summary: Requested execution of a sharper variant probe and recorded a second mechanism it exposed locally. In the new scenario the owner commits X and fails after its Commit reaches only one live peer, so replica 2 holds X COMMITTED while replica 3 recovers the same instance holding no command. Local native feedback shows the recovery proposing the NOOP although replica 2's prepare reply carried X with status COMMITTED, and then stalling: adopting that COMMITTED status into lb.status makes the guard at epaxos/epaxos.go:870 discard replica 4's reply, so the restarted phase-1 proposal never reaches its fast quorum and replica 3's instance stays pre-accepted with no accept or commit emitted. That mechanism is recorded as a new behavior with a new source range (epaxos/epaxos.go:847-895) and a new active question about whether the stall repeats identically on the executor's retry, with the two comparisons (recovery proposes the quorum-reported value; the recovering replica reaches a decided state) declared for the controller's receipt. This turn's unfinished work: the interpretation of that receipt and confirmation that the observed incompleteness is the target's status-guard interaction rather than harness scheduling.
